title: I Posted the Nursery Plant-Hold Photo After They Resold My Fiddle

parts.text: I paid a 72-hour plant hold on a fiddle-leaf at 11:40 a.m. On hour 40 the same tag was on a stranger's cart. The hold policy at the register said: PAID HOLDS STAY IN THE CAGE. NO FLOOR RESALE. I was twenty-nine, apartment light, holding the hold receipt. Clerk Bo said, "Fiddles want to travel." I pointed at the cage. He rang the stranger. "Travel is sales." I photographed the tag on the cart, the policy, and my receipt. Then I posted the still to the nursery's hold-claim email. At 11:47 the manager asked why Bo's name was on a hold-resale ticket.
parts.cliffhanger_hint: The manager can see my paid tag on a stranger's cart against the cage policy.

social.video_title: They resold my held fiddle-leaf — Part 1/2
social.description: Hour 40, a traveling fiddle, and a cage policy. I emailed the still. Would you have picked a new tree?

parts.text: Bo called it a mixup until the tag barcode matched my receipt. I printed the ticket, the policy, and the photo. The fiddle went back to the cage. Bo told the greenhouse the policy was always about optics. Optics is a word clerks use when a leaf is in a cart still. Hold policy now has a second line: TRAVEL IS NOT RESALE. I pick up on hour 72. Bo cages. The soil finally waits.

social.video_title: Travel is not a floor resale — Part 2/2
social.description: Hold-resale ticket, fiddle caged again, and a second line at the register. Was sales ever hour 40?
